status: CONFIRMED — reviewed by Siddhant against Bottom Plate (SE-004-052) and Top Plate (RKSE-004-053) real labeled data
description: Scoped to the 10 manual feature labels that actually appear on the two labeled parts (not the full 46-label app vocabulary — the rest are unused so far). Maps each to CAPP's internal feature_type for the strict, no-partial-credit scorer: a CAPP cluster only counts as correct if (1) it's a clean 1:1 boundary match to exactly one manual annotation, AND (2) its predicted feature_type equals this table's answer for that label. Labels with mapping=null are excluded from type-scoring for a documented reason (see 'reason'); do not silently score them as either pass or fail.

mappings.status: confirmed for Top Plate; open question on Bottom Plate
mappings.reason: GAP-01 fixed 2026-09-14: classify_features.py's boss branch now checks has_cap_plane. A capless Forward cylinder is a convex edge/corner round, not a real boss. Verified: Top Plate's 4 Radius instances are clean 1:1 matches correctly typed 'round' (radius ~5mm, Forward/convex). GAP-04 also fixed same day (detect_slots false-merge) — Bottom Plate's 2 Radius instances are now clean 1:1 matches too, BUT they turned out to be Reversed/concave (radius 0.75mm, depth 1.125mm, tiny) and classify as 'blind_hole', not 'round'. That's plausibly a CORRECT call for that geometry, not a CAPP bug — these look like a genuinely different physical feature from Top Plate's large convex corner rounds. Open question for Siddhant: were Bottom Plate's 2 'Radius' instances mislabeled (should be something else), or does CAPP need a small-concave-recess-vs-blind-hole distinction too? Left as-is pending an answer rather than force-mapped.

Most-used label overall (26 combined instances). Per Siddhant (2026-09-14): a Vertical Planar Face is cut by the SIDE of the tool (wall), a plain Planar Face is cut by the BOTTOM of the tool (floor) — a real tool-engagement distinction CAPP's feature_type enum doesn't encode at all. CAPP is inconsistently calling these clusters either planar_face or pocket depending on incidental face_area/perp_wall_count thresholds (POCKET_MAX_AREA_MM2=500, POCKET_MAX_PERP_WALLS=8 in classify_features.py) with no recession/offset check — e.g. Top Plate: all 14/14 clean-1:1 instances of this label predicted 'pocket'; Bottom Plate: 2 predicted planar_face, 4 predicted pocket. This re-surfaces the already-known deferred rule R1 (SESSION_STATE priority queue: 'pocket floor vs open face — blocked until adjacent_cluster_ids + centroid populated for plane-seeded clusters'), now with concrete real-part evidence.

Verified against real STEP geometry (face centroid vs bounding-box extent, 2026-09-14): some instances are genuinely open faces at the bbox boundary (Bottom Plate face 8 at z=0; Top Plate face 14 at z=10 — correctly planar_face), others are genuinely recessed 2.5mm below the top surface (Bottom Plate faces 61/63/66/68/70/73 at z=5.0 vs bbox zmax=7.5 — CAPP's 'pocket' answer for these is plausibly correct). The label itself doesn't disambiguate floor-vs-open the way 'Vertical Planar Face' unambiguously means wall. A single taxonomy entry would be wrong for one case or the other. Does not change today's score: no instance of this label is a clean 1:1 match on either part (all merged/split across clusters) — revisit if/when a clean match needs grading.

Verified against real geometry (2026-09-14): on both parts this is ONE continuous semi-cylindrical groove (identical radius=3.1mm, depth, and axis across all matched CAPP clusters) that CAPP's clustering split into 2-3 fragments, then classified inconsistently — the multi-face fragments as 'slot', the lone single-face fragment as 'fillet'. Same fragmentation class of bug as GAP-02, not a taxonomy ambiguity: no fixed answer is correct while clustering doesn't group the whole feature together.

CAPP's 'slot' type drops the obround-vs-rectangular shape distinction. Per Siddhant (2026-09-14): shape matters, not just feature identity — do not credit CAPP with 'correct' when it can't represent the shape. Excluded rather than scored as automatic fail or pass.
Same reasoning as Obround Through Slot — CAPP's 'pocket' type drops the freeform shape qualifier. Excluded from scoring, not scored as pass or fail.

pipeline_gaps_logged.title: No concave/convex check in fillet/boss classification
pipeline_gaps_logged.detail: cluster_features.py now sets has_cap_plane on bore/boss clusters (True only if growth found a validated closing cap plane). classify_features.py's boss branch uses it: a capless Forward cylinder is a convex 'round' (or 'round_angled'), not a 'boss'. Verified on real data: Top Plate's clean 1:1 boundary-match count for this label's instances all now correctly classify as 'round'. See rule_sheets/08_manual_label_taxonomy.json 'Radius' entry.

pipeline_gaps_logged.title: No side-wall vs bottom-floor / recession check on plane clusters (re-surfaces deferred rule R1)
pipeline_gaps_logged.detail: planar_face vs pocket is decided by face_area + perp_wall_count only, with no check of tool-engagement direction (side vs bottom) or actual recession (offset from neighboring surface). Needs adjacent_cluster_ids + centroid populated on plane-seeded clusters (blocked per SESSION_STATE R1) plus a recession/offset computation. NOT fixed by GAP-01's work — different mechanism (plane clusters, not cylinder clusters).

pipeline_gaps_logged.title: Elongated single-radius features get fragmented and classified inconsistently
pipeline_gaps_logged.detail: A single continuous semi-cylindrical groove (same radius/depth/axis throughout) gets split into multiple clusters at face boundaries, and the fragments receive different feature_type answers (slot vs fillet) depending on how many faces landed in each fragment. NOT fixed by GAP-01's work — this is a clustering-growth/fragmentation issue, not an orientation or classification issue.

pipeline_gaps_logged.title: detect_slots() merges unrelated same-size bore-family clusters with no adjacency check
pipeline_gaps_logged.detail: detect_slots() matched ANY two bore-family clusters with equal radius, parallel axis, and equal depth into a 'slot' -- with no check that they were actually adjacent/connected. Found on Bottom Plate: two independent 'Radius' instances (faces 21, 23 -- both Reversed/concave, not convex as first assumed) share no real wall of their own, only a distant shared neighbor (the part's 7837mm^2 background face), and were merged purely on matching numbers. Fixed by adding detect_slots(clusters, config, G) with a real connectivity check (_cluster_connecting_faces): the two candidate clusters must be directly adjacent, or share a connecting face smaller than config.large_face_area_threshold (rules out two unrelated features that just happen to both sit on the same big stock face). Verified: faces 21/23 are now two separate clean clusters instead of one fake slot. Bottom Plate's clean 1:1 boundary-match count rose 8 -> 14.

pipeline_gaps_logged.title: Single-face bore fillet-detection DDR threshold catches genuine through-holes
pipeline_gaps_logged.detail: The old fillet check gated on cluster.get('has_perpendicular_walls', False), a field hardcoded False for every bore cluster (only ever computed for plane clusters) -- vacuously true for any deep single-face bore, so DDR>1.0 alone decided 'fillet'. Fixed with a real signal: adjacent_wall_plane (cluster_features.py) is True only if a neighbouring Plane's normal is perpendicular to the cylinder's own axis (a real wall to blend into). classify_features.py's fillet branch now gates on this; a deep single-face bore with no adjacent wall falls to 'through_hole' instead. Verified: Bottom Plate's 4 real 'Through hole' instances (faces 24-27, DDR=1.125) now correctly classify 'through_hole'; the genuine 'Semi cylindrical profile' fillet (DDR~8.7, has a perpendicular wall neighbour) is unaffected. feature_extraction_accuracy 9.4% -> 10.3% overall.
